text:
Rain had thinned to a drizzle on the steps of Wexcombe Town Hall when the pen finally met paper, and a small crowd, gathered more out of loyalty than curiosity, watched a long-running question come to an end. The Aldermoor hoard, which had passed through uncertain custody for years, now belongs in the care of the Wexcombe Museum.

The transfer was confirmed on 14 March 2024, when the Aldermoor Hoard Custody Agreement was signed at a public ceremony. Dr. Imelda Tarrowby, Head of Acquisitions at the museum, announced the arrangement.

The collection comprises 1,327 items, among them silver coins, torcs and brooches. Each piece carries the quiet weight of whoever buried it and never returned. For Wexcombe, the hoard is now an inheritance as much as an acquisition.
